title: India needs innovative strategies to eliminate TB
description: Context: Recent data from the Indian Council of Medical Research’s (ICMR) landmark PreVenTB Phase III clinical trial has revealed that two newly evaluated indigenous vaccines, VPM1002 and Immuvac, provide significant protection against extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB). About India needs innovative strategies to eliminate TB: Current Global and National Status of TB: Key Challenges in Eliminating Tuberculosis: India’s bold fight against tuberculosis cannot be won by waiting for a single, perfect global breakthrough. The success of the indigenous PreVenTB trial shows that moderately effective, scalable tools like VPM1002 are ready to provide immediate protection against the hidden, lethal burden of extrapulmonary TB. India has one of the highest burdens of Tuberculosis (TB) globally, and ensuring an adequate supply of quality-assured drugs is crucial for effective treatment. Examine the major impediments to ending TB in India. (250 words)

title: The power of mangroves over seawalls
description: Context: The landfall of Cyclone Dana near Bhitarkanika on Odisha’s coast has highlighted the powerful protective role of coastal mangroves over expensive, engineered infrastructure. About The power of mangroves over seawalls: What is Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA)? Key Data and Statistics on India’s Coastal Adaptation: Key Features of Mangroves as Climate Shields: Challenges Associated with India’s Coastal Adaptation Policy: India’s heavy reliance on rigid, concrete seawalls provides temporary relief but ultimately shifts and worsens long-term erosion risks along its fragile coastline. The proven success of mangrove systems during intense cyclones demonstrates that investing in natural capital is both economically sound and socially equitable. Mangroves hold crucial resources that can help protect the rich and diverse biosphere. Nature-based solutions offer a holistic and sustainable approach to protect mangroves in India. Analyse. (250 words)

title: Service Sector as Growth Engine
description: This editorial is based on “Gauging the services sector” published in The Financial Express on 05/06/2026. It argues that the sector's expanding influence on GDP and employment necessitates a more precise, high-frequency tool to effectively monitor and guide economic policy. For Prelims: Gross Value Added (GVA), Trade Deficit, Global Capability Centres (GCCs), Intellectual Property, Gross Non-Performing Asset (GNPA), Global Innovation Index (2025), e-Shram Portal, ASUSE 2025, Balance of Payment, Gig Workers. For Mains: Key Achievements of the Service sector in India and Associated issues, Measures needed to strengthen the service sector in India. The services sector has evolved into the primary engine of global and Indian economic growth, necessitating more sophisticated tracking mechanisms to capture its expanding influence on GDP, employment, and exports. Despite achievements in exports and financial stability, challenges like "jobless" growth, informality, and regional disparities persist. Strategic governance and upskilling are essential to sustain this momentum and ensure inclusive development.
